N01.name: Laurel Marquise Necklace
N01.note: it is held in a woman's open hand in a shop, in front of other necklaces on a maroon velvet board: ignore the hand, the board and every other necklace, and take only the marquise-stone necklace lying across the palm.
N01.lock: A MARQUISE LEAF NECKLACE: one continuous line of clear MARQUISE-cut (navette, pointed oval) faceted stones, each about 5x10mm in its own gold four-claw setting. The stones are grouped in THREES: in every group the three marquise stones are set on a SLANT, side by side and slightly overlapping like three leaves on a stem, all leaning the same way. Each group of three is joined to the next by one small gold link, so the line reads as a row of leaf clusters with a tiny gap between them. Warm polished gold tone settings.
N01.neg: Every stone is a pointed marquise, never round, never pear, never baguette; the stones lie on a slant in groups of three, never in one straight end-to-end row, never in pairs; no pendant, no drop, no plain chain section; clear stones only, no colour.
N01.scale: Each marquise stone is about 10mm long and 5mm wide; the line of stones is about 9mm wide, about half the width of a finger.
N01.wscale: Worn, the line of marquise clusters lies around the base of the neck like a slim sparkling collar, about half a finger wide, never a heavy bib.
N01.place: laid on the top face in a long smooth curve, the slanted clusters of three legible, part of the line running over the cube's front edge
N01.macro: three or four of the slanted marquise clusters in their gold four-claw settings and the small gold links between them
N01.palm: the necklace gathered in the open palm, the line of marquise clusters lying across the palm and over the fingers
N01.pscale: Each marquise stone is about as long as the width of a fingernail; the line of stones is about half a finger wide.

N02.name: Soleil Petal Pendant
N02.note: it is held between a woman's fingers over a black velvet tray, with a white pouch and cards behind it: ignore the hand, the tray and the packaging, and take only the pendant and its fine chain.
N02.lock: A HALF-SUNBURST PETAL PENDANT on a fine gold snake chain: at the top centre ONE round brilliant-cut clear stone, about 7mm, held up in gold claws; SEVEN slender polished gold PETALS fan out below and beside it only, close together like the rays of a rising sun: one points straight left, one down-left, one steeply down-left, one straight down, one steeply down-right, one down-right and one straight right, each a narrow open loop of polished gold about 10mm long with a rounded tip, all springing from just under the stone. Nothing rises above the stone: the upper half of the pendant is bare and the snake chain passes behind the stone. The pendant is about 28mm across and about 16mm tall.
N02.neg: Exactly seven petals, all in a half fan from left round the bottom to right, exactly as IMAGE 1 shows; no petal above the stone, never a full circle of petals, never a pinwheel; the petals are slim open loops, never solid flat leaves, never pave, never sharp star points; one clear stone only; no second pendant.
N02.scale: The pendant is about 28mm across, about the width of a large coin; the stone is about 7mm, smaller than a fingernail.
N02.wscale: Worn, the pendant is small: about 28mm across, a little more than half the width of her lips, its stone about 7mm; it sits just below the hollow of the throat on the fine chain.
N02.place: laid flat on the top face, the chain in a soft V and the pendant at its point, its seven petals fanned below the stone
N02.macro: the round clear stone in its claws at the top and the seven polished gold petals fanning out below it
N02.palm: the pendant lying flat in the centre of the open palm, its fine chain trailing over the fingers
N02.pscale: The whole pendant is about as wide as two fingers side by side; its stone is about half as wide as one finger.
N02.measure: 2 Nov, from the owner's photo: the pendant spans about 1.8 finger widths (about 27 to 30mm), the stone about 0.28 of the pendant (about 7 to 8mm). The first worn and palm shots drew it about 1.7 to 2 times that and were shrunk by edit.

N03.name: Pearl Crescent Pendant
N03.note: it lies in a white plastic pouch held in a woman's hand: ignore the hand, the pouch and its reflections, and take only the pendant and its chain. The pearl is a smooth round white shell pearl with a soft lustre. In this photo the chain happens to lie looped around the left side of the pendant inside the pouch: that loop is only how it was packed, NOT part of the design; ignore it.
N03.lock: A PEARL CRESCENT PENDANT on a fine gold box chain with a small sliding bead: ONE round white pearl, about 10mm, with a soft creamy lustre; a slim CRESCENT of about eight small round clear stones, each in its own little gold collar, curves around the RIGHT side and the BOTTOM of the pearl, from the top right round to the bottom left, like a new moon; the upper LEFT side of the pearl is bare, just the smooth pearl. The pendant hangs from ONE small gold bail at the top, where the chain passes through; from the bail the fine chain runs straight up on both sides, like any pendant necklace.
N03.neg: One pearl only, round and white, never pink, grey or golden; the crescent of small clear stones follows only part of the pearl's edge, never a full halo; the chain NEVER wraps around the pearl, never forms a loop or a gold rim on the pearl's left side and never crosses over the pendant; no other drop; the chain is a fine square box chain, never a rope or cable, never chunky.
N03.scale: The pearl is about 10mm, about the size of a fingernail; each crescent stone is about 2mm.
N03.wscale: Worn, the pendant is small: the pearl is about 10mm, about a fifth of the width of her lips, and the whole pendant with its crescent about 14mm; it sits just below the hollow of the throat on the fine box chain.
N03.place: laid on the top face, the chain in a soft V and the pearl crescent pendant at its point
N03.macro: the white pearl and the curve of small clear stones in their gold collars beside it
N03.palm: the pendant lying in the centre of the open palm, its fine box chain trailing over the fingers
N03.pscale: The pearl is about the size of one fingernail; the whole pendant is no wider than one finger.

A16.name: V-Bar Teardrop Necklace
A16.note: it lies in a white plastic pouch held in a hand: ignore the hand and the pouch, and take only the necklace.
A16.lock: A V-BAR TEARDROP NECKLACE ON A WHEAT CHAIN: a dense gold WHEAT chain (a spiga chain) about 3.5mm wide, built of tiny narrow links shaped like grains of rice, each with a bright flat cut face, set in a tight CHEVRON, two rows of grains leaning in towards each other along the chain like the grains on an ear of wheat, packed so tightly that no holes or gaps show, so the chain reads as a slim, softly rounded cord of glittering slanted grains; at the centre front the chain turns into TWO short smooth polished gold TUBE BARS, each about 15mm long and as wide as the chain, which meet at a point to form a sharp V; from the point of the V hangs ONE clear PEAR-cut faceted stone, about 10x13mm, its narrow tip at the TOP joined to the point of the V, its round end at the BOTTOM, held in fine gold claws; the stone is about two thirds as wide as one bar is long.
A16.neg: The chain is a dense wheat chain of slanted rice-grain links with no holes, never open links with holes, never a curb or Cuban chain, never a cable, box, rope or Figaro chain, never a smooth flat herringbone or snake ribbon; two plain polished tube bars form the V, never a plain bail on the chain; one pear stone, clear, never a pearl.
A16.scale: The pear is about 13mm long and 10mm wide, about the size of a fingernail; each bar of the V is about 15mm long and the chain about 3.5mm wide, about a third of the pear's width.
A16.wscale: Worn, the wheat chain lies on the collarbones with its slanted grains glinting, the polished V points down at the centre and the clear teardrop hangs from its point just below the hollow of the throat; the pear is about a fifth of the width of her lips.

A16.macro: the two polished gold bars meeting in a V, the clear pear-cut stone hanging point up from it, and the slanted rice-grain links of the wheat chain running away from each bar
A16.palm: the necklace lying in the open palm, the polished V and the teardrop in the centre, the wheat chain over the fingers
A16.pscale: The pear is only about two thirds of the width of one of her fingertips and each polished bar about as long as the top joint of her finger; the chain is about a fifth of a fingertip's width.
A16.measure: Owner's 2 Nov photo (refs/A16_full.jpg), sent again on 3 Nov with the supplier's line 390x5 1,950: the chain is not a herringbone. It was first read as a curb chain of faceted oval links; at 6x (refs/A16_chain6x.jpg, second 3 Nov note) it is a dense wheat (spiga) chain of rice-grain links leaning in a chevron, with no holes, and the open curb drawn earlier on 3 Nov was replaced. Against the bars (about 170 px each, taken as 15 mm, as on 2 Nov): the chain is about 40 px (about 3.5 mm) and the pear with its claws about 108 px wide and about 140 px tall below the V (about 10 x 13 mm); the 2 Nov copy said 3 mm and 8 x 11 mm. A13.name: Slim Pave Huggies
A13.detname: IMAGE 2 is a flat DRAWING of ONE huggie seen exactly side-on and the authority on its SHAPE and proportions: a rounded square as deep as it is tall, a slim band, the row of stones down its front edge and the hinge seam in its top edge; it is a drawing, so take only its outline and proportions from it, never its flat colours.
A13.note: they hang through two holes in a small white card printed STAINLESS STEEL, inside a clear plastic bag held in a hand, each seen at an angle with its back half behind the card: ignore the hand, the bag, the card and its printing, and take only the pair of earrings.

Down the FRONT edge, from the hinge at the top to the bottom corner, runs ONE row of about ten round clear stones, each held up in its own small raised gold claws so the stones stand proud of the band and almost touch, with tiny gold beads between them; right beside it, along the OUTER edge of the band, away from the opening, runs a SECOND row of tiny round clear stones, so the sparkle wraps round the edge; the bottom, the back and the inside are plain polished gold; a hinged click post in the top edge.

A13.place: the two huggies standing upright side by side on the top face, closed, each turned so its rounded-rectangle side outline faces the camera with the stone row on its front edge
A13.macro: ONE huggie standing upright on its flat bottom edge, seen from the side so its whole rounded-rectangle outline is in frame: its straight front edge with the row of round stones in raised gold claws, and the row of tiny stones beside it on the outer edge, runs straight up one side, the plain polished back edge up the other, the hinged post at the top
A13.palm: the pair of huggies lying side by side in the centre of the open palm, each closed, the stone rows facing up

The first packshot (A13_H) drew a 3:1 paperclip and was replaced. Five packshots were drawn: the generator will not make the outline square (A13_Hs edit 2:1, A13_Hq 2.5:1, the drawing-guided edit A13_Hd 2.4:1); A13_Hg, a fresh packshot guided by the flat outline drawing refs/A13_shape.jpg, came out about 1.9:1, which matches the outline the huggies show in the owner's photo, and was approved. 3 Nov setting (owner: 'Check diamond setting and change it'; refs/A13_set.jpg): the round stones stand in raised claws, almost touching, and a second row of tiny stones runs along the OUTER edge of the band, outside them; the 2 Nov gallery had sunk one small row in a railed channel. A15.pscale: Each heart is about 20mm, a little wider than one of her fingertips.

Both give about 20 mm; the 31 Oct listing said 11 mm. The band of two stone rows is about 0.13 of the heart's width, about 2.5 mm. The 31 Oct photos drew one row of larger stones in silver tone; the stock is gold tone, as the owner said ("the heart is gold").

C2.name: Clover Garland Necklace, Red
C2.note: it lies folded in half inside a long clear plastic sleeve on black velvet, its two halves side by side, under a white card printed Stainless Steel; more sleeves of the same necklace lie behind it: ignore the sleeves, the card, its printing and the velvet, and take only the one necklace in the front sleeve.
C2.detname: IMAGE 2 is a closer view of three of the same clovers and the small gold rings between them.
C2.lock: A CLOVER-LINK NECKLACE: one single continuous line of about thirty-five IDENTICAL small four-petal clovers, linked one after another by a tiny round gold jump ring, all the way round the neck. Each clover is four ROUND faceted bright clear RED stones in a two-by-two quatrefoil, each stone in its own round gold cup edged with a fine BEADED milgrain rim of tiny gold dots, and ONE tiny clear stone at the very centre where the four petals meet. Along the necklace every clover sits like a diamond, one petal pointing forward along the line, one back and one to each side, and each gold ring joins the tip of one clover's petal to the tip of the next. Warm gold tone cups and rings.
C2.neg: Every clover has exactly four round red stones plus the tiny clear centre stone: never five petals, never heart-shaped or pointed petals, never solid gold, enamel or mother-of-pearl clovers. The clovers never touch or fuse into a band: a small gap with one gold ring between each pair. Every petal stone is a clear bright red as in IMAGE 1, never pink, never orange, never dark maroon or brown, never opaque, never mixed with other colours. The beaded rims stay fine gold dots. No pendant, no drop, no plain chain section in front.
C2.scale: Each clover is about 10mm across, the size of a small fingernail; each round stone is about 3.5mm, the size of a peppercorn; the necklace is a delicate line only 1cm wide.
C2.wscale: Worn, the necklace is a delicate line only 1cm wide lying round the base of the neck and across the collarbones; each clover is about 10mm, the size of a small fingernail and about a fifth of the width of her lips, so about eighteen clovers run across the front from one side of the neck to the other; never a heavy collar or a bib.
C2.pscale: Each clover is about 10mm, about two thirds of the width of one of her fingertips, and the coil covers under half the palm.
C2.place: laid on the top face in a long smooth curve, the clovers legible one by one, part of the line running over the cube's front edge
C2.macro: a short run of three or four of the red clovers and the small gold rings joining them
C2.palm: the necklace gathered in a small loose coil in the open palm, a run of the red clovers lying across the palm and the rest of the line spilling softly over the fingers
C2.measure: Owner's 3 Nov photo (f87bb96a): five sleeves, the front one holding one necklace folded in half. A clover is about 78 px and a stone about 27 px (stone/clover 0.35, as on the Clover Garland Bracelet, whose clover was measured at about 10 mm against a thumb), so about 7.8 px per mm. Each half of the fold runs about 1,800 px, about 23 cm, so the necklace is about 42 to 46 cm with the clasp, about 34 clovers. The length is an estimate: to confirm with a tape. 3 Nov evening: on the Clover Garland Bracelet's worn photos a clover is about 0.22 of the lip width (about 10 mm, as its copy says); C2_W1_a and C2_W2q_a drew it at about 0.31 and 0.33 (about 15 mm), so both worn frames were rebuilt (comp.py garland, C2_W1g at 0.70 and C2_W2qg at 0.67), with 17 and 19 clovers along the visible neck.

A14.name: Solitaire Charm Huggies
A14.note: the two huggies lie in a small clear plastic bag on black velvet, the left one open on its hinge, with ONE charm lying between them (the second earring's charm is hidden under its hoop): ignore the bag, its creases and the velvet, and take only the earrings.
A14.detname: IMAGE 2 is a closer view of the same two huggies and the charm.
A14.lock: A PAIR OF SOLITAIRE CHARM HUGGIES: each earring is a CHUNKY plain polished gold huggie hoop about 13mm across with a THICK, wide, flat-faced band, about 2mm thick and 3mm wide, so its round opening is only about three quarters of its outer width; it closes with a hinged snap and carries ONE charm at the bottom. The charm is threaded ON the hoop: a CHUNKY SQUARE polished gold TUBE about 4mm, about a third of the hoop's outer width on each side, that the band passes through, and below it ONE small round gold jump ring holding ONE round brilliant-cut clear stone about 6.5mm across, about HALF the hoop's outer width, in four fine gold claws. The stone hangs free below the hoop and can swing.
A14.neg: The hoop is plain polished gold with a thick band, never a thin wire, never a wide flat cuff, never pave, never textured; the charm hangs free from the bottom of the hoop on its square tube and one ring, never fixed onto the front of the hoop, never a stud, never a chain of rings; the stone is round and held only by four fine claws, never in a cup, bezel or halo, never pear or square; exactly one charm per earring, clear stones only.
A14.scale: Each hoop is about 13mm across, about the width of a fingertip; the round stone is about 6mm, half the hoop's width, smaller than a fingernail; the whole earring is about 22mm long from the top of the hoop to the bottom of the stone.
A14.wscale: Worn, the slim hoop hugs the earlobe closely, about as wide as the lobe itself, and the charm hangs just below the lobe: the square tube at the bottom of the hoop and the round stone, about half the hoop's width, below it; the whole earring is about a third of the height of the ear, a small bright drop, never a big hoop.
A14.pscale: Each hoop is about as wide as one of her fingertips and each stone about half that; the pair covers well under half the palm.
A14.place: the two earrings standing side by side on the top face, each hoop closed, the charms hanging forward from the bottom of the hoops
A14.macro: one earring: the slim plain polished hoop, the square polished tube threaded on it and the round clear stone in its four fine claws hanging from the tube's small ring
A14.palm: the pair of earrings lying side by side in the centre of the open palm, hoops closed, each charm laid out below its hoop
A14.measure: Owner's 3 Nov photo (15d03401): the closed hoop is about 150 px across and its band about 25 px thick; the stone is about half the hoop's width in the 3x crop (refs/A14_det.jpg); the hoop is taken as about 13 mm, the size AL-449 was booked at, giving a stone of about 6 mm and a drop of about 22 mm. Nothing in the bag gives a second scale, so these are estimates. 3 Nov afternoon, measured again with both hoops and the loose charm lying flat at one distance (refs/A14_det.jpg): the hoop's opening is about 0.73 of its outer width (band about 2 mm), the square tube about a third of the hoop and the stone about 0.5 to 0.54 of it, so about 6.5 to 7 mm on a 13 mm hoop; the approved packshot A14_Hs2_b gives the earring about 23.5 mm long.

B1.name: Orb Cable Cuff
B1.note: the photo shows TWO identical cuffs lying overlapped inside a small clear plastic bag on a white card, beside a thumb: ignore the bag, its creases and glare, the white card, the thumb and the second cuff, and take only ONE cuff.
B1.detname: IMAGE 2 is a closer view of the open ends of the same cuff: the two wrapped collars, the two balls and the twist of the cable; the cable running down behind and between the two balls belongs to the SECOND cuff in the bag, so ignore it: the opening between this cuff's two balls is empty.
B1.lock: AN OPEN CABLE CUFF BRACELET: ONE length of gold tone twisted CABLE about 4mm thick, made of many fine strands twisted together into tight, even diagonal spiral ridges like a rope, bent into an open C, very slightly oval, about 6.5cm across inside. Each of its TWO ends finishes with a short COLLAR of about three turns of wrapped gold wire, a little thicker than the cable, and then ONE smooth plain round gold BALL about 8mm across, about twice the cable's thickness. The two balls face each other across a small empty opening of about 1.5cm. The whole cuff is one pale, light yellow gold tone with a soft polished sheen, exactly the colour of IMAGE 1.
B1.neg: The cable is a twisted rope of fine strands with even diagonal ridges, never a smooth plain wire, never a chain, never a braid, never hammered; exactly two balls, one at each end, both plain smooth gold, never pearls, never stones, never pave, never engraved, never caps with points; the collars are plain wrapped wire, never set with stones; no clasp, no hinge, no charms; ONE cuff only, never two stacked, never a closed bangle.
B1.scale: The cuff is about 6.5cm across inside, about as wide as a slim wrist; the cable is about 4mm thick, thinner than a pencil; each ball is about 8mm across, the size of a small pea.
B1.wscale: Worn, the cuff circles the wrist a little loosely and is about as wide as the wrist itself; the cable is a slim line, about a fifteenth of the wrist's width, and each ball is about the size of a small pea, never a big chunky bangle.
B1.pscale: The cuff is nearly as wide as her palm; each ball is smaller than her fingertip and the cable is thinner than her little finger's nail is wide.
B1.wear: the opening on the TOP of the wrist facing camera, so the two balls sit face to face on the back of the wrist
B1.place: lying flat on the top face of the cube, seen from a little above so its whole open C reads, the opening at the front towards camera with the two balls facing each other
B1.macro: one end of the cuff: the twisted cable's fine spiral strands, the wrapped wire collar and the smooth round ball, with the second ball just across the small opening
B1.palm: the cuff lying flat in the centre of the open palm, its opening towards the fingers and the two balls facing each other
B1.measure: Owner's 3 Nov photo (b7bdaf33: two cuffs overlapped in a bag beside a thumb, refs/B1_full.jpg and the 2x crop refs/B1_det.jpg). On the front cuff: outside width about 857 px, cable about 44 px, each ball about 100 px, the gap between the two balls about 173 px; the thumb nail is about 185 px and the thumb about 250 px wide at the nail. Taking the thumb as about 21 mm wide (about 11.5 to 12.5 px per mm, allowing for the thumb sitting nearer the camera), the cable is about 3.5 to 4 mm, the balls about 8 to 8.5 mm, the inside about 6.1 to 6.8 cm and the opening about 1.4 to 1.5 cm. Nothing in the bag gives a second scale, so these are estimates, written as cable 4 mm, balls 8 mm, inside 6.5 cm, opening 1.5 cm.
